evidence_scope: summary-level vCluster mocker throughput and client-placement diagnostic, not a promotion-grade request-ID, tail-SLO, or GPU audit
integrity_checks: Frozen plan SHA256 and trace SHA256 checked before Job creation.
Exact Nix bundle, 1/8/8/32 serving topology, and 20+20 gateway threads checked before Job creation.
All 24 Pods completed on the three planned CPU nodes, eight per node.
Every raw export reports AIPerf 0.12.0, fixed-schedule mode, zero exported errors, and no cancellation.
All client logs prove mmap-cache HIT and tokenizer/composer skip; Job Pods mounted the digest-named reader-overlay ConfigMap.
limitations: All 24 AIPerf clients flagged replay-schedule degradation; the nominal offered schedule was not faithfully delivered.
The two-node point belongs to a previous series, so the numerical 8.47% difference cannot be attributed causally to placement.
AIPerf summary export has no request-level JSONL, so request-ID completeness and tail-metric recomputation are not independently auditable.
Client nodes had 15 running other-namespace Pods at both occupancy snapshots; no synchronized neighbor or client CPU series was collected.
The gateway cgroup CPU sample missed the measured phase and is not usable for saturation analysis; vCluster Metrics API was unavailable.
No user SLO was specified, and workers were synthetic rather than production GPU workers.
decision: The clean absolute 8951.78 RPS result disproves 8252.72 RPS as a hard one-gateway ceiling, but scheduling degradation and cross-series comparison prevent a placement-effect or gateway-capacity claim. A stronger test needs less-contended load generation, faithful replay, and synchronized per-stage CPU profiles.
